items.title: Art Farmer — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He’s not like Mr. Jones, not that kind of stuff.

ctx.x: He was a fine guy. He was straight ahead. I spoke to him on the telephone sometime. He seems to be the same guy. Of course, he’s in another atmosphere now [laughs]. But, he’s still Quincy. He’s not like Mr. Jones, not that kind of stuff. I met Gigi in the band, I met Benny Golson in the band, Monk Montgomery, James Cleveland, Alan Dawson, good people in the band. That was a good time too. It was nice to meet these guys. We were like a family. Big bands usually develop cliques, so there were two cliques in this…
You mentioned your first recorded composition was “Farmer’s Market.” Had you already started writing before this? Had you started composing?
